title: Bar chart sheet
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: Sound (Misty Mountain, Sierra and How Can We Change a Sound?)
source: Seeded from science/y4 lesson 20 (Bar chart sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 20: Measuring volume: decibels and our ears. To understand how volume is measured in decibels and why loud sounds can harm our ears

blocks.text: Label both axes, choose a scale, and draw the bars with a ruler, with gaps between them.

questions.q: A quiet room is 40 dB; talking is 60 dB. Which is louder and by how much?
questions.model: Bigger number is louder: 60. How much more? 60 minus 40 is 20. So talking is louder by 20 dB.

questions.q: Why do workers with drills wear ear defenders?
questions.a: To protect their ears from loud noise

questions.q: What unit is volume measured in?
With an adult, measure three sounds with a sound meter app (a quiet room, the kettle boiling from 2 m away, talking). Record in dB and order them.
questions.a: Pupils' own readings, for example quiet room 35 dB, talking 60 dB, kettle 65 dB
questions.model: Teacher measures the quiet classroom on camera: 'About 38 dB.' Records it.

questions.q: Draw a bar chart of your three readings.
Why might two people get different readings for the same sound?
questions.a: Different distances, phones or background noise; keep distance the same.

questions.q: Big question: how could you prove which room is noisiest?
questions.a: Measure each room in decibels at the same distance and time.
